call_points.text: India multi-channel growth to stay elevated for the rest of FY27 on RocketBees, FC Qwik and offline assortment changes.
Of the 280 bps gross-margin loss in Q4, only 20 bps recovered in Q1; full recovery seen by Q3-Q4.
Crude-linked and rupee-depreciation cost increases to be fully passed on to customers by end of Q2.
About 100 net store additions planned this fiscal, with FY28 expansion to be better.
Offline GMV grew 15% in Q1 on the width-to-depth assortment change.
International adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to 7% of revenue from 10%; no breakeven date given.
GlobalBees revenue was flat on a planned brand warehouse transition, expected to complete in Q2 with growth back from Q3.
Pre-school segment revenue rose 47% to ₹19 Cr and adjusted EBITDA 65% to ₹5 Cr; target is 1,000 preschools in a couple of years.
Analyst pressed on international breakeven timing; management declined to give a quarter, saying only "sooner than you think".
Analyst asked for the profitability gap between diapering and non-diapering; management gave no number, only that diapering is not loss-making.
International adjusted EBITDA losses fell 33% YoY in Q4FY26 and 35% in FY26.
Two horizontal e-commerce players that entered UAE and KSA in 2024 keep promotional activity elevated.
Globalbees core categories grew 28% in FY26 with ₹92 Cr adjusted EBITDA post corporate expenses.
India multichannel was PAT and free cash flow positive in FY26; consolidated free cash flow was also positive.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune dated January 30, 2026, under the Income-Tax Act, 1961, wherein an addition of Rs. 93,57,99,520/- has been made to the total income of the Company for AY 2022-23 w.r.t Transfer Pricing adjustment of Rs. 10,84,95,240/- and addition on account of disallowance of ESOP expenses: Rs. 82,73,04,280/-, and consequently a tax demand of Rs. 31,36,30,330/- has been raised.In continuation to Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune, Company made an application to the Authority and on verification of the case records by the said Authority, the Company is in receipt of the rectification order and demand notice from the Authority wherein the total income of the Company for AY 2022-23 is now recomputed as Rs. 52,54,110/-, thereby reducing the amount of demand for AY 2022-23 from Rs. 31,36,30,330/- to Rs. 38,37,210/- (i.e. by Rs. 30,97,93,120/-).
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income Tax Department Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal with Hon. ITAT on 26th March 2026.

penalties.details: The Court issued an order imposing a penalty of Rs. 25,000/-
penalties.impact: The Company has paid the penalty amount of Rs. 25,000 on 28.04.2026 and the matter stands closed.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The Office of the Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication), Mumbai, via order dated January 13, 2026, had demanded a differential duty along with redemption fine and penalty on the Company amounting to Rs. 6,56,58,134/- (exclusive of applicable interest under Section 28AA of the Customs Act, 1962), ("Order") primarily on interpretational grounds in respect of alleged violation in connection with failure to comply with procedural aspects of documentation relating to country of origin of the imported goods, under Asia-Pacific Trade Agreement (APTA) framework.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Office of the Commissioner of Customs (Adjudication), Mumbai
tax_litigation.status: The Company has filed an appeal against the said order before the Customs Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) on April 11, 2026.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: On October 25, 2024, the Department has issued notices under section 148 of the Act for the A.Y. 2018-19, A.Y. 2019-20, A.Y. 2020-21 and A.Y. 2021- 22 to make re-assessment/re-computation under Section 147 of Income Tax Act. The ACIT had passed an order under section 148A(d) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 ("the Act") treating the case of the Company fit for reopening of assessment proceedings and for issuance of notice under section 148 of the Act, for AY 2018-19, AY 2019-20, AY 2020-21, and AY 2021-22. Consequently, a notice was issued under section 148 of the Act for the aforesaid years in case of the Company, and the assessment proceedings were reopened. The Company has filed a writ petition before the Bombay High Court, wherein the validity of reopening of the assessment proceedings has been challenged. The case was listed for hearing before the Hona'ble Bombay High Court on June 16, 2025 The matter was heard, and the Hona'ble High Court has given an interim relief by granting a stay on the reassessment proceedings till the time of disposal of the petition. The case was listed for hearing before the Hona'ble Bombay High Court on July 16, 2025 and the matter has been heard and disposed by the High Court, and the reassessment proceedings were quashed.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income Tax Department Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Central Circle 1(1), Pune
tax_litigation.status: Pursuant to the subsequent developments arising from the amendments to the applicable provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, the matter relating to the reassessment proceedings, which had previously been quashed by the Hon’ble Bombay High Court, is presently sub-judice before the Hon'ble Bombay High Court.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune dated January 30, 2026, under the Income-Tax Act, 1961, wherein an addition of Rs. 93,57,99,520/- has been made to the total income of the Company for AY 2022-23 w.r.t Transfer Pricing adjustment of Rs. 10,84,95,240/- and addition on account of disallowance of ESOP expenses: Rs. 82,73,04,280/-, and consequently a tax demand of Rs. 31,36,30,330/- has been raised. In continuation to Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune, Company made an application to the Authority and on verification of the case records by the said Authority, the Company is in receipt of the rectification order and demand notice from the Authority wherein the total income of the Company for AY 2022-23 is now recomputed as Rs. 52,54,110/-, thereby reducing the amount of demand for AY 2022-23 from Rs. 31,36,30,330/- to Rs. 38,37,210/- (i.e. by Rs. 30,97,93,120/-). On March 26, 2026, the Company filed an appeal with Hon'ble ITAT against the Assessment order and a corresponding notice of demand served on the Company by the office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune.
tax_litigation.opposing_party: Income Tax Department Office of the Assistant Commissioner of Income Tax, Pune
tax_litigation.status: The Hon'ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal ("ITAT"), vide its order dated September 29, 2026, adjudicated upon the tax and transfer pricing matters pertaining to the Company for AY 2022-23. Pursuant to the said order, the corporate tax adjustment amounting to Rs. 82,73,04,280/- relating to disallowance of ESOP expenses, has been deleted in its entirety by the ITAT in favour of the Company. Further, out of the total Transfer Pricing adjustment of Rs. 10,84,95,240/-, an amount of Rs. 3,78,41,525/- has been deleted in favour of the Company and the balance Rs. 7,06,53,715/- has been remanded to the Transfer Pricing Officer (“TPO”) for fresh consideration and adjudication in accordance with law. The company shall file suitable submissions during the penalty proceedings, requesting that the no penalty ought to be levied on disallowance of ESOP expenditure since the corresponding additions have been deleted by ITAT.

timeline.summary: Shareholders approved Ms. Saloni Jain Rana (DIN: 11489732) as Non-Executive & Non-Independent Director via Postal Ballot on May 04, 2026, with 98.90% voting in favor.
Brainbees Solutions filed the ICRA Monitoring Agency Report for Q4 FY26 showing ₹919.47 Cr utilized out of ₹1,666 Cr IPO proceeds with no deviations.
Brainbees Solutions reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹8,547.94 Cr and approved further overseas investments from IPO proceeds.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,162.67 Cr, net loss to shareholders ₹30.31 Cr (against a loss of ₹76.74 Cr a year earlier).
On 13 August 2026 Brainbees Solutions (FirstCry) held its Q1FY27 earnings call
NCLT New Delhi dismissed the Section 7 IBC application of ₹64.92 Cr filed against material subsidiary Globalbees Brands.
Brainbees announced an extension of the timeline to November 30, 2026, for GlobalBees to divest its 51.54% stake in Mush Textile.
Globalbees Brands acquired an additional 14.23% stake in JW Brands Private Limited for ₹18.68 Cr on October 30, 2026.
